hook.text: Google's Project Jacquard wove touch-sensitive threads into a Levi's jacket. You answer calls by tapping your sleeve.

buildup.text: Smart textiles embed sensors, LEDs, or conductive fibers directly into fabric.

discovery.text: Medical smart fabrics can monitor heart rate, body temperature, and muscle activity without wearable devices.

twist.text: The military funds most smart textile research. Soldiers' uniforms may soon detect chemical weapons and change color.

climax.text: The privacy implications are staggering. Clothing that monitors you also creates data that others can harvest.

punchline.text: Your next shirt might know more about you than your doctor.

quiz.question: What was Google's smart textile project called?

details.summary: Smart textiles embed technology directly into fabric — monitoring heart rate, changing color with temperature, or harvesting solar energy. From military applications to health monitoring, clothing is evolving from passive covering into active, responsive technology.
details.whyItMatters: Smart textiles blur the line between clothing and technology, potentially transforming garments into health monitors, communication devices, and energy sources we wear daily.
takeaways: Smart fabrics can monitor vital signs like heart rate and temperature
Color-changing textiles respond to heat, light, or electrical signals
Military and medical sectors drive most smart textile research

faq.question: What can smart textiles do today?
faq.answer: Current smart textiles can monitor heart rate and breathing, regulate body temperature, charge devices via solar cells woven into fabric, and change color on command. Google and Levi's collaborated on a jacket with touch-sensitive fabric that controls a smartphone.

faq.question: When will smart clothing become mainstream?
faq.answer: Basic smart textiles like moisture-wicking and UV-protective fabrics are already mainstream. More advanced features like health monitoring are entering consumer markets through athletic wear.
